title: Four Against the Great Old Ones - a nestled deep dive
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=73a6CtNTac4

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens a "nestled deep dive" inside the ongoing Four Against Darkness series: Four Against the Great Old Ones by Marco Arnaudo and Andrea Sfiligoi, plus its two expansions, Carcosa Rising and The Dawning Horror. Four investigators criss-cross a map of the United States, spending days as a currency to travel, rest, recruit and investigate. Three clues pinpoint which Great Old One waits at the end, and it must all be settled within forty days. Everything is a d6 against a target number with exploding sixes, but the bookkeeping is heavy enough that Daniel recommends the PDFs over the physical books so you can print fresh location sheets each game. He likens the feel to Eldritch Horror in book form, or an Inkle game like 80 Days.

Carcosa Rising is his favourite of the three: a modular grab-bag of alternate Catskills, New Orleans and New York, Perilous Journeys tables, a King in Yellow sub-boss, and an Underground Temple module that drops a little Four Against Darkness dungeon crawl into Chicago. The Dawning Horror offers five paragraph adventures for a single investigator and henchmen, with levelled-up professions carrying forward. Woven throughout is a reading list: Robert M. Price's Chaosium anthologies, the Hastur Cycle, Lovecraft's Dream Cycle, and Chambers' "The Repairer of Reputations", which Daniel names his favourite short story of all time. He still slightly prefers Alone Against Fear, but calls the replay-value criticism overstated.

----

Daniel says this is a game you should "play to lose" your first dozen times. Do you enjoy solo games where losing well is the point, or do you need a winnable path?
